title: Protective effect and mechanism of taxifolin 7-rhamnoside extracted from Hypericum japonicum against LPS/D-GalN-induced acute liver injury.
authors: Ran, Hengxing; Wen, Yan; Qin, Yiebi; Kang, Kaiwen; Wu, Zhengrong; Li, Yifan; Wang, Yu; Wu, Rihui; Li, Dongli; Ang, Song; Gan, Lishe; Jin, Jingwei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物TAX对急性肝损伤的保护机制，涉及分子对接与MD模拟但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: This study aims to identify the most primary hepatoprotective compound from Hypericum japonicum and elucidate its underlying mechanisms of liver protection. This study screened 15 compounds from Hypericum japonicum against D-GalN-induced AML12 cell injury, identifying TAX (Compound 8, taxifolin 7-rhamnoside) as the most hepatoprotective. This study indicates that TAX reduced AST, ALT, and MDA levels, while enhancing SOD and GSH levels in D-GalN-induced AML12 and LPS/D-GalN -induced liver. In addition, TAX attenuated LPS/D-GalN-induced hepatic injury by lowering inflammatory infiltration and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6 and NO) levels. Network pharmacology analysis revealed common targets between TAX and drug-induced liver injury, forming a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network. Functional enrichment (GO/KEGG) and molecular docking indicated strong binding affinity between TAX and AKT1, confirmed by molecular dynamics simulations. Western blot analyses that TAX ameliorated inflammation and oxidative stress through down-regulating the AKT/NF-kappaB pathways and up-regulating Nrf2/HO-1 pathways in vivo, TAX inhibited apoptosis via up-regulating Bcl-2 and down-regulating Bax in vitro. Collectively, this study demonstrates that TAX ameliorates LPS/D-GalN-induced ALI by attenuating hepatocyte apoptosis, inflammatory responses, and oxidative stress.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在从地耳草（Hypericum japonicum）中筛选最具保肝活性的化合物，并阐明其保肝作用机制。本研究针对D-GalN诱导的AML12细胞损伤，筛选了地耳草中的15种化合物，鉴定出TAX（化合物8，花旗松素7-鼠李糖苷，taxifolin 7-rhamnoside）为最具保肝活性的成分。研究表明，在D-GalN诱导的AML12细胞及LPS/D-GalN诱导的肝脏中，TAX降低了AST、ALT和MDA水平，同时增强了SOD和GSH水平。此外，TAX通过降低炎症浸润和促炎细胞因子（TNF-alpha、IL-6和NO）水平，减轻了LPS/D-GalN诱导的肝损伤。网络药理学分析揭示了TAX与药物性肝损伤之间的共同靶点，并构建了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络。功能富集分析（GO/KEGG）和分子对接表明TAX与AKT1之间具有强结合亲和力，并通过分子动力学模拟得到验证。Western blot分析显示，在体内，TAX通过下调AKT/NF-kappaB通路和上调Nrf2/HO-1通路改善炎症和氧化应激；在体外，TAX通过上调Bcl-2和下调Bax抑制细胞凋亡。综上，本研究证明TAX通过减轻肝细胞凋亡、炎症反应和氧化应激，改善LPS/D-GalN诱导的急性肝损伤（ALI）。
